 Stock Market Highlights: Sensex declines 143.21 points to settle at 73,709.69; Nifty drops to 22,811.35 
 Share Comments Stock Market Highlights: Sensex declines 143.21 points to settle at 73,709.69; Nifty drops to 22,811.35
 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Oct 21, 2026, 16:14:52 IST SUMMARY Indian equity benchmarks ended lower on Wednesday as concerns over rising crude oil prices erased early gains, with losses in auto, metal and banking stocks weighing on the broader market. The Sensex closed at 73,709.69, down 143.21 points, or 0.19 per cent, while the Nifty 50 declined 77.60 points, or 0.34 per cent, to settle at 22,811.35. 
 Brent crude prices climbed 1.31 per cent to $110.15 per barrel, fuelling concerns about imported inflation, corporate profitability and the country's import bill. 
 The information technology sector was the standout performer, with the Nifty IT index rising 2.52 per cent, making it the only major sectoral index to finish higher. In contrast, the Nifty Auto index declined 1.99 per cent, while the Nifty Metal index fell 1.97 per cent. Realty stocks lost 1.57 per cent and media shares declined 1.24 per cent. 
 Banking and consumer stocks also ended under pressure. The Nifty Private Bank index fell 1.16 per cent, while the FMCG index shed 0.89 per cent. 
 In the commodities market, gold declined 0.49 per cent to Rs 1,45,803 per 10 grams, while silver prices dropped 1.15 per cent to Rs 2,09,061 per kg. 
 Global markets presented a mixed picture, with most major Asian benchmarks closing higher. South Korea's KOSPI surged 3.19 per cent, Taiwan's weighted index advanced 1.27 per cent and Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.98 per cent. Hong Kong's Hang Seng bucked the trend, slipping 0.95 per cent. 
 Together, these factors are expected to shape the direction of stock market in the days ahead. Track TOI’s coverage on BSE Sensex and Nifty50 to know which way stock markets are headed: Live Events 
 16:14 (IST) Oct 21 IT stocks lead Nifty gainers; Bajaj Finance, BSE among top losers IT stocks led the Nifty 50 gainers, with Infosys rising 3.30%, HCL Technologies gaining 3.21%, Tech Mahindra climbing 3.13% and TCS advancing 2.77%. On the losing side, Bajaj Finance fell 3.27%, followed by BSE (-2.63%), Eternal (-2.45%), Eicher Motors (-2.43%) and Trent (-2.41%).

 16:10 (IST) Oct 21 IT stocks lead Sensex gainers; Bajaj Finance, Eternal top losers IT stocks led the Sensex gainers, with HCL Technologies rising 3.40%, Infosys gaining 3.31%, Tech Mahindra climbing 3.21% and TCS advancing 2.68%. On the losing side, Bajaj Finance fell 3.33%, followed by Eternal at 2.71%, Trent at 2.32%, Axis Bank at 2.11% and NTPC at 1.99%. 15:45 (IST) Oct 21 Sensex declines 143.21 points to settle at 73,709.69; Nifty drops 77.60 points to 22,811.35 14:57 (IST) Oct 21 Nifty tumbles over 200 points, slips below 22,700 as 41 stocks trade in red The Nifty 50 fell sharply , declining 213.45 points, or 0.93 per cent, to 22,675.50 in afternoon trade. The benchmark opened higher at 23,016.00 against its previous close of 22,888.95 but reversed early gains to slip below the 22,700 mark. Market breadth remained firmly negative, with 41 of the 50 index constituents trading in the red and only nine advancing, reflecting broad-based selling pressure. 13:51 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: Sensex plunges over 500 points, Nifty50 slips below 22,800 The BSE Sensex was trading 553.65 points, or 0.75%, lower at 73,299.25 while NSE Nifty 50 was down 212 points, or 0.93%, at 22,764.10. 
 13:22 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: Top laggards on BSE Sensex The selling pressure was broad-based, with most Sensex constituents trading in the red. Bharti Airtel and LT were among the relatively resilient stocks, slipping 0.04% and 0.22%, respectively. Bajaj Finance was the biggest laggard, falling 3.32%, followed by Eternal, down 3.20%, and Trent, which declined 2.70%. Axis Bank dropped 2.23%, while Maruti Suzuki fell 2.20%. Other notable losers included Bajaj Finserv (2.16%), IndiGo (2.14%), NTPC (2.06%) and BEL (1.89%). Kotak Mahindra Bank, Adani Ports and HDFC Bank also traded lower, shedding 1.72%, 1.53% and 1.51%, respectively. Daily Puzzles

NSE Nifty50 also traded lower, sipping below the 22,800 mark to 22,739.65, down 149.30 points or 0.65%. 11:46 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: Sensex slips in red, Nifty50 trades below 22,900 mark Dalal Street gave up its gains in later trade, with both benchmark indices slipping into the red. The BSE Sensex was trading at 73,768.44, down 84.46 points or 0.11%, while the NSE Nifty 50 stood at 22,831.20, declining 58 points or 0.25%. 10:51 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: Rupee trades strong against US dollar but crude prices limit gain
 Rupee inched higher against the US dollar on Wednesday, jumping 29 paise to trade at 94.62 in early deals. The rally came as foreign currency inflows linked to the Jio IPO and gains at the Dalal Street supported the currency. At the same time, support from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also helped rupee, although rising crude oil prices and a firm dollar restricted its advance. Read full story › 10:06 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: BSE Sensex trades at 74,300, 440 points up The BSE Sensex pared some of its early gains but was still trading 447.12 points, or 0.61%, higher at 74,300.02. IT stocks continued to lead the gains, with Infosys rising 3.42% to Rs 1,168.60. TCS advanced 2.32% to Rs 2,518, while HCL Technologies gained 2.24% to Rs 1,407.85. Tech Mahindra was up 2.23% at Rs 1,817.70. 09:44 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: BSE Sensex soars 800 points, NSE Nifty50 trades above 23,100 BSE Sensex jumped over 800 points to hit 74,682.19 in early trade on Wednesday, while Nifty 50 climbed 229.40 points, or 1%, to 23,118.35. The benchmarks traded higher, supported by optimism over a possible India-US trade deal, although elevated crude oil prices and US bond yields are expected to weigh on market sentiment. 09:37 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: NSE Nifty50 jumps 1% in early trade BSE Sensex jumped to 74,596.26, up 743.36 points, or 1.01%. NSE Nifty 50 was also gained 1% to trade 212.15 points up at 23,036.85.
 Among the top gainers on the Nifty50, Infosys led the pack, rising 3.14% to Rs 1,166.15. UltraTech Cement gained 2.54% to Rs 10,920, while TCS advanced 2.43% to Rs 2,520.80. Reliance Industries climbed 2.13% to Rs 1,227.60, and ICICI Bank rose 1.81% to Rs 1,406.00.
 09:23 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: Top gainers on BSE Sensex in early trade BSE Sensex rose 677.67 points, or 0.92%, to 74,530.57 in early trade. Infosys led the gainers, climbing 3.08%, followed by UltraTech Cement, which advanced 2.51%. TCS also gained 2.50%, while Reliance Industries rose 2.10% and HCLTech advanced 2.01%. Tech Mahindra was up 1.48%, followed by ICICI Bank at 1.26% and Larsen & Toubro at 1.12%. Power Grid and ITC each gained 0.96%, while Kotak Mahindra Bank rose 0.80% and Bharti Airtel advanced 0.74%. 09:19 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: Sensex jumps 500 points, Nifty50 inches past 23,000 Dalal Street began Wednesday on a strong note, with BSE Sensex jumping over 550 points and NSE Nifty50 rising above 23,000 levels.BSE Sensex rose 527.21 points, or 0.71%, to 74,380.11 while NSE Nifty 50 gained 147.90 points, or 0.65%, to trade at 23,036.85. 08:53 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: Top stocks to watch on October 21
 Somil Mehta, head of retail research at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, has identified three stocks as his top sell recommendations for Wednesday. Read full story › 08:51 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: Where are BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty50 headed on October 21 Dalal Street is likely to open higher on Wednesday, with GIFT Nifty futures at 23,017, indicating a positive start for the Nifty 50 after Monday’s close at 22,888.95. Markets were shut on Tuesday for a local holiday. Optimism around a possible US-India trade deal could support sentiment, while Bajaj Finance shares will be in focus after the lender reported a 28.7% year-on-year rise in quarterly profit. However, elevated crude oil prices remain a key risk. Higher energy costs could increase India’s import bill, strain the fiscal deficit and weigh on corporate profitability, potentially limiting gains in domestic equities. 08:50 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: Asian markets trade in green; Nikkei gains over 1%, Kospi adds 200 points Asian stocks rose on Wednesday, supported by gains on Wall Street as early corporate earnings pointed to strong profits and boosted investor confidence. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climbed 1.5%, led by a 4% rise in Korean shares, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 advanced 1.3%. S&P 500 e-mini futures gained 0.3%. Regional markets have steadied after last week’s sharp selloff, although concerns around artificial intelligence investments, elevated oil prices and borrowing costs continue to weigh down sentiment. 08:49 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market today: Crude holds near $110 per barrel mark Oil prices rose on Wednesday amid concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East, with traders monitoring risks to Red Sea shipping and threats to Saudi oil infrastructure. Brent crude futures gained 85 cents, or 0.78%, to $109.64 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude rose 76 cents, or 0.78%, to $98.58. The gains followed declines in the previous session, when Brent settled at $108.79 after touching a five-month high of $111.99. Reports of attacks on vessels and Saudi infrastructure have heightened concerns over energy supplies, although earlier hopes of mediation between Iran and the US had weighed on prices. 08:48 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market recap: Rupee inched higher against the greenback in previous trading Rupee pared its initial gains to settle 2 paise lower at 94.91 against the US dollar on Monday, snapping a six-session winning streak. The currency came under pressure from weakness in Dalal Street, a recovery in crude oil prices and continued foreign institutional investor outflows. It opened at 94.90, touched an intraday high of 94.75 and a low of 94.97 before closing at 94.91. Despite the decline, rupee appreciated around 2% during the week ended October 16, supported by RBI measures to manage dollar demand. 08:47 (IST) Oct 21 Stock market recap: BSE Sensex, NSE Nifty50 ended last session in red Benchmark indices ended sharply lower on Monday, giving up gains after two consecutive sessions of rallying. BSE Sensex fell 876.37 points, or 1.17%, to settle at 73,852.90, while NSE Nifty 50 declined 257.20 points, or 1.11%, to close at 22,888.95. The selloff was led by private banking stocks, particularly Axis Bank and HDFC Bank, amid weak global cues. Axis Bank fell 3.85% despite reporting a 39.4% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 7,704.67 crore in the second quarter of FY27. Indian stock markets closed lower on Wednesday after giving up early gains, as rising crude oil prices and selling pressure in several sectors weighed on investor sentiment. The BSE Sensex declined 143.21 points, or 0.19 per cent, to settle at 73,709.69, while the Nifty 50 fell 77.60 points, or 0.34 per cent, to close at 22,811.35.
Brent crude rose 1.31 per cent to $110.15 per barrel, raising concerns over imported inflation, corporate margins and India's import bill. The surge in oil prices also heightened pressure on the rupee.
Information technology stocks bucked the broader market trend, with the Nifty IT index gaining 2.52 per cent to emerge as the only major sectoral index to close in positive territory. Auto and metal stocks led the losses, with the Nifty Auto index falling 1.99 per cent and the Nifty Metal index declining 1.97 per cent.
The Nifty Realty index dropped 1.57 per cent, while the Media index fell 1.24 per cent. The Private Bank and FMCG indices declined 1.16 per cent and 0.89 per cent, respectively.
In the commodities market, gold prices fell 0.49 per cent to Rs 1,45,803 per 10 grams, while silver declined 1.15 per cent to Rs 2,09,061 per kg.
Meanwhile, most major Asian markets ended higher. South Korea's KOSPI gained 3.19 per cent, Taiwan's weighted index rose 1.27 per cent and Japan's Nikkei 225 advanced 0.98 per cent. Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 0.95 per cent.
